commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Moves the Kimi-K3.1-Pro GB300 AgentX presets to the configurations of [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#5109](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5109) (head `b2326892`): image `kimi-k31-mc-f4c9618`, Dynamo `ec06c09e72`, and the released draft `Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark` at revision `e4e6e626`. InferenceX's sign-off check requires a merged vLLM recipe that documents the submission's serving settings, as #67719, #68213 and #68220 did for InferenceX#5069.

## Claims

| Preset | Points | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `gb300_agentx_pd` | 44, 104 (new) | 1P5D only: 5 draft tokens at 44, 4 at 104 with an adaptive 4096-token long-prefill threshold on prefill; the image's opt-in TP8 + DCP8 decode paths (`K31_*`) on decode. The 56-client 1P5D and 1P3D points are dropped. |
| `gb300_agentx_pd_hybrid` | 256, 448 | 5 draft tokens (were 6 and 4); decode graphs in multiples of 6 up to 1536; EPLB on prefill at both points and on decode at 448 |
| `gb300_agentx_pd_dep32` | 960 | 5 draft tokens (was 4) with decode graphs up to 192; `--prefix-match-unit 512`; EPLB on both roles; the draft's sliding-window tail store and hits; a 2048 MB indexer logits budget on prefill; a Mooncake master that evicts 5% at a 0.98 watermark |
| `gb300_agentx_c1` | 1 | `--prefix-match-unit 768`; the image's opt-in concurrency-1 decode paths (`K31_*`) |

- All four serve the released draft at revision `e4e6e626`. `--prefix-match-unit` is 1408 on the TP8 + DCP8 and hybrid presets. The runbooks give the released draft's golden acceptance lengths: 3.46, 3.81 and 4.16 for 4, 5 and 7 draft tokens.
- `gb300_agentx_pd_dep16` (352 clients, #4907) renders as before. Its runbook now names its own Dynamo revision and lists the PD-preset settings it does not use. Non-GB300 presets are unchanged.

## Validation

- **Flag by flag against #5109** (head `b2326892`). For each point, the effective config (the base recipe deep-merged with the point's override) was compared role by role with the commands the recipes renderer produces (`renderCommand` in strict mode, vllm-project/recipes main).
  - The TP8 + DCP8 and hybrid points (44, 104, 256, 448) match in every arg and env var on both roles.
  - The DEP32 and concurrency-1 points match except for what the builder renders: the DEP launch flags, and the Dynamo request-plane env of the aggregated lane, which its runbook lists.
  - The benchmark-only `--served-model-name` and `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE` are left out on purpose.
- The frontend commands and Mooncake master options in the runbooks were checked against each lane's `frontend` and `services` blocks.
- `gb300_agentx_pd_dep16` renders identically to main.
- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this repo>/recipes` passes from vllm-project/recipes main. pre-commit passes.

## Details

- **Image-only env.** `K31_*`, `VLLM_DFLASH_SWA_TAIL_STORE`, `VLLM_DFLASH_SWA_TAIL_HITS` and `VLLM_SWA_FINE_GRAINED_HITS` exist only in the pinned image's vLLM build (`0.1.dev25380+gf4c96184b`), not in vLLM main, and the runbooks say so. `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` is in main.
- **Point keys.** `c56` and `c56_1p3d` are removed with #5109's point set, and `c104` is new.
- No other open PR edits the GB300 presets. This PR touches only the GB300 section and `meta.date_updated`.

**Update (InferenceX#5109 head `5db09f14`).** #5109 now serves the concurrency-960 DEP32 point with one DEP32 prefill worker instead of two DEP16 prefill workers, on the same 16 trays, and the second commit matches `gb300_agentx_pd_dep32` to it: prefill spans eight trays (`--data-parallel-size 32`, so each rank holds half the routed experts of a DEP16 rank) with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 85899345920` per rank, the point is now 1P1D, and the runbook no longer starts a second prefill worker. Prefill EPLB, the prefill env and the Mooncake master options are unchanged. Compared flag by flag with `override_1p1d_dep32`, both roles match except for the builder's DEP launch flags, as before; the other presets render exactly as in the first commit, and `validate-source.mjs` and pre-commit pass.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Apply the video processor frame caps when loading videos
commits.pr_body:
The chat path loads videos through the Qwen3-VL video backend, whose default `max_frames` is a hardcoded 768, so a model whose HF video processor declares a smaller cap (LFM3-Omni-2B: 384) gets more frames than its processor would sample.
The loaders now default `max_frames`/`min_frames` to the model's HF video processor values; `--media-io-kwargs` and per-request `media_io_kwargs` still override.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KV Offload] Avoid waking idle FS workers on job completion
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

FS job completion broadcasts to idle workers because workers and `wait_idle()`
share one condition. Give drain waiters a separate condition on the same lock
so completing a job does not wake workers when no tasks are available.

## Claims

- Preserve task dispatch, drain and shutdown behavior without another lock.
- Reduce FS worker CPU overhead; measured store batches also use less engine
  CPU and finish sooner. No consistent end-to-end reload change is established.

## Validation

- Regression fails before the fix and passes after it.
- `uv run --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py`:
  **38 passed, 13 skipped** (optional C extension unavailable).
- Drain/shutdown checks passed 20 times per implementation; scoped pre-commit passed.

GB10, bf16, eager/TRITON_ATTN, multiprocessing, O_DIRECT, 16+16 FS workers,
2 GiB GPU KV / 512 MiB CPU staging. Batches contain eight 1,024-input/32-output
requests, at most four concurrent. Four A/B runs per model balance pool creation
order; four SmolLM2 A/A runs provide calibration. All **4,608 requests** have
matching output tokens and FS job/block counts.

**Mean ms per eight-request batch, before → after:**

| Model / workload | Batch latency | Engine CPU | FS worker CPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SmolLM2-135M / store | 785.8 → 762.6 (-2.95%) | 825.2 → 797.5 (-3.36%) | 39.6 → 19.9 |
| OPT-125M / store | 312.6 → 300.7 (-3.83%) | 349.9 → 335.3 (-4.16%) | 39.7 → 26.5 |
| SmolLM2-135M / reload | 719.6 → 718.7 (-0.13%) | 739.1 → 736.1 (-0.40%) | 17.5 → 13.5 |
| OPT-125M / reload | 284.6 → 281.8 (-0.99%) | 294.9 → 290.4 (-1.53%) | 21.8 → 17.5 |

Latency measures `LLM.generate`; engine CPU includes FS CPU and final draining,
excluding snapshot collection. Store gains hold in both creation orders
(95% latency-change CIs: [-3.50%, -2.38%] / [-4.39%, -3.27%], engine/block
bootstrap).

## Details

Workers keep using the task condition. Drain waiters use a second condition
under the same mutex, notified when the final job completes. Shutdown notifies
both conditions. Queue priorities, enqueue notifications and I/O are unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve reused ARC prefixes during running-request eviction
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow up #67098 by including reused T1 chunks in ARC's running-request tail-first eviction, using the same request-access hook as LRU.

## Claims

- Avoid leaving a newly stored suffix behind an evicted, reused prefix under concurrent store pressure.
- Preserve ARC's request-completion frequency promotion and existing active chunk ownership.

## Validation

Tested on main plus this patch.

- `python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py -q`: 88 passed, 14 warnings in 12.72s. The modified regression covers load/store reuse under both policies: 4 passed, 84 deselected, 14 warnings in 0.64s; both ARC cases fail without the fix.
- Scoped pre-commit checks passed.

SmolLM2-135M-Instruct on GB10, ARC with 240 MiB CPU / 2 GiB GPU KV cache, four staggered 3,073-token requests. GPU-only prefix-cache resets force CPU reloads while retaining the CPU cache. Results from three alternating runs per version:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Replay cached tokens (every run) | 0 | 1,664 |
| One-token replay latency, median (range), ms | 268.3 (256.5–271.1) | 133.9 (132.9–134.4) |
| Concurrent generation time, median (range), s | 2.856 (2.754–2.895) | 2.868 (2.865–2.886) |

Generated tokens and logprobs were identical between versions in all three paired runs.

## Details

The CPU manager reports reused prefixes through `on_request_access`, but ARC inherits the no-op hook and groups only newly inserted chunks. Once a prefix load completes, eviction can discard that prefix before the same request's new suffix, making the remaining suffix unusable for prefix lookup.

Register resident T1 keys with known positions in the existing running-request ordering, retaining any existing owner rather than transferring shared keys between running requests. This adds tracking once per observed key and reuses the existing eviction and cleanup paths. The benefit depends on retaining part of the request: pressure that evicts the entire request cannot improve its subsequent hit rate.

---

## Overview

OpenAI's `tool_choice: {"type": "allowed_tools", ...}` lets a client keep one stable tool list and change only which tools the model may call in a given turn, so the prompt (and the prompt cache) stays the same across turns. The Rust frontend returns 400 for it on both Chat Completions and Responses. This PR supports it on both: every declared tool stays in the rendered prompt, and the allowed subset restricts only the call grammar.

## Claims

- Chat Completions accepts the nested OpenAI shape (`{"type": "allowed_tools", "allowed_tools": {"mode": "auto" | "required", "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": ...}}]}}`); Responses accepts its flat shape (`mode`/`tools` at the top level) and echoes the resolved choice in the response.
- Under `required` the model can only call a tool in the subset; under `auto` it can answer in text or call a tool in the subset. Every declared tool, request-level and message-scoped, still reaches the chat template.
- An allowed name that matches no declared tool, a `required` choice with an empty list, and non-function refs are a 400. An empty `auto` list allows no call: tool parsing is off as under `none`, while the tools stay in the prompt.
- The Chat Completions `tool_choice` object is now modeled as a serde-tagged `ToolChoiceObject { Function, AllowedTools }`, mirroring `ResponseToolChoiceObject`, instead of untagged variants carrying `type` as a string checked by match guards; an object with an unknown `type` is rejected at deserialization.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), at `b8059e1385` (merged `main` `2f170a0fed`):

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2898 passed, 13 skipped
```

The first commit on its own also passed workspace clippy and nextest on its original base `92fd8cc668`.

New tests:

- `chat_allowed_tools_restrict_the_call_grammar` (route, mock engine, `qwen3_coder` parser, xgrammar backend): the structural tag sent to the engine admits only the allowed function in both modes, and both functions under plain `required`. Lowering `AllowedTools` to plain `required` fails it.
- `resolved_tool_context_keeps_every_tool_under_allowed_tools`: initial and message-scoped tools all stay available to the renderer, and the choice lowers to XGrammar's allowed-tools choice.
- `resolved_tool_context_resolves_choice_by_tool_availability` gains the unknown-name and empty-`required` cases.
- `tool_choice_none_drops_parsed_tool_calls` gains the empty allowed list: a parsed call is dropped as under `none` (keeping parsing on surfaces it).
- `auto_allowed_tools_call_only_the_allowed_tools` (Beam grammar snapshot): only the allowed tool and the answer, no undeclared-name branch (the branch reappears without the fix).
- `renders_tool_choice_as_an_instruction` (Inkling2): gains `AllowedTools` (keeps all declared tools and injects no tool-choice instruction).
- `prepare_chat_request_lowers_allowed_tools_tool_choice`, `prepare_chat_request_rejects_invalid_allowed_tools`, `allowed_tools_choice_resolves_names_and_keeps_every_tool` (namespace resolution and echo), `allowed_tools_choice_rejects_unsupported_tool_types`.

Matcher check (not committed): the `auto` structural tag from the route test, compiled with XGrammar 0.2.9 against the `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` tokenizer, accepts plain text, the allowed call, and text followed by the allowed call, and rejects `<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>` with or without leading text.

## Details

- **Python today.** Chat Completions rejects the shape at schema validation (`tool_choice` accepts only `none`/`auto`/`required`/named). Responses accepts the type, but `get_json_schema_from_tools` treats it like `auto`, so calls are not restricted (vllm-project/vllm#60585 fixes that for Python Responses). This PR therefore goes beyond Python parity on purpose.
- **Prompt stays fixed.** Filtering the rendered tools to the allowed subset (as vllm-project/vllm#51535 does for Rust chat) would change the prompt whenever the subset changes and defeat prefix caching, which is the point of the OpenAI feature.
- **Layering.** `vllm-chat` gets `ChatToolChoice::AllowedTools { mode, names }` (mode is XGrammar's `AllowedToolsMode`, re-exported). `ResolvedToolContext::new`, where every other tool choice is resolved for both endpoints, validates the names against the effective tools and leaves the tool lists untouched. The choice lowers to XGrammar's `ToolChoice::AllowedTools`, which `normalize_tool_choice` / `build_structural_tag` already support for every builder and model-owned grammar, so no grammar code is added. The server only lowers each endpoint's wire shape; Responses resolves flat refs like a named choice (`ResponsesToolNames::resolve_choice`, so a namespaced function can be listed by its local name).
- **Model-owned renderers and grammars.** Beam's grammar treats a `required` allowed-tools choice as forcing a call, like `required` and named choices, and admits undeclared tool names only under plain `auto`. Kimi K3's native encoder injects no tool-choice message for it, matching the reference `encoding_k3.py`, which only reacts to `required` and `none`. Inkling 2's native renderer likewise keeps every declared tool and injects no tool-choice instruction for it, keeping the prompt prefix fixed.
- **`finish_reason`.** `is_named_tool_choice` stays false, so a call ends with `tool_calls`, as under `required`.
- **Limitation.** As for `required` and named choices today, the restriction needs a parser with a tool grammar and the `xgrammar` structured-outputs backend. Otherwise (the `guidance` backend, or native parsers without a tool grammar such as Harmony and Inkling) the request runs unconstrained, with the existing one-time warning for the backend case.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#51535 supports `allowed_tools` on Rust chat by filtering the rendered tools, which changes the prompt (see above); vllm-project/vllm#60585 is the Python Responses fix.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Pass image kwargs through the OpenCUA processor
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`OpenCUAProcessor.__call__` calls the image processor without any kwargs, so `min_pixels`, `max_pixels` and `size` from `--mm-processor-kwargs` or a request are silently ignored. Profiling uses the shared Qwen2-VL sizing, which does apply them. With `max_pixels=512**2` the profiled budget is 334 tokens per image, while a 1920x1080 image still produces 2,691.

This PR passes the image kwargs to the image processor with `_merge_kwargs`, like the other vendored processors (Bagel, Ovis, Isaac). It also sets `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = False` on OpenCUA. Without that, the routing would break the model: OpenCUA inherits the flag from Qwen2.5-VL, but its own vision tower is built without `input_norm`. Today it only works because the processor also drops the `do_rescale=False, do_normalize=False` that vLLM sends for device normalization.

#67111 lists this OpenCUA bug as deferred. This PR is independent of it: the two PRs share no files, the merge is clean, and the tests below pass on the merged tree.

## Claims

- Size kwargs now reach the OpenCUA image processor, at init, per request and scoped under `images_kwargs`. With each form used on its own, the processed token count matches the sizing helper's prediction and Qwen2.5-VL's count.
- Default outputs are unchanged. On an L4, greedy output token ids match main for all 5 test images.
- With `max_pixels=512**2`, OpenCUA uses 308 to 330 image tokens per image instead of 391 to 2,646, and still answers all 5 test prompts correctly.

## Validation

**GPU, one L4.** Wheel of main 2c1fc9b3d3. Only `opencua.py` differs between the arms (sha256 checked). Requests are greedy, 64 tokens, with the checkpoint's chat template. Image tokens are counted as `<|media_placeholder|>` ids in the prompt:

| image | main: image tokens, answer | this PR | main, `max_pixels=512**2` | this PR, `max_pixels=512**2` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rendered text "access code is ORANGE 2468" (1280x720) | 1196, "ORANGE 2468" | same ids | 1196 (ignored) | 312, "ORANGE 2468" |
| rendered "Submit" button (1024x768) | 999, "Submit" | same ids | 999 | 315, "Submit" |
| `stop_sign` asset | 1426, "A red stop sign is in front of a Chinatown." | same ids | 1426 | 330, "A red stop sign is in front of a black SUV." |
| `cherry_blossom` asset | 2646, "...cherry blossoms in full bloom, with the Tokyo Skytree..." | same ids | 2646 | 308, "The Tokyo Skytree is visible through a tree with pink blossoms." |
| solid red (640x480) | 391, "red" | same ids | 391 | 315, "red" |

The `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = False` line is needed. With only the routing change, the processor returns raw `uint8` pixels, OpenCUA's vision tower doesn't normalize them, and the model answers "123456", "SHOP NOW", "...a red and white cartoon character...", "...a stack of white boxes..." and "white" for the same 5 images.

To reproduce, on one GPU with this branch or main installed:

```
python 1_opencua_l4_check.py --child default
python 1_opencua_l4_check.py --child max_pixels
```

Script and raw logs: https://gist.github.com/subhashpolisetti/998c972d5e006d801d84bf89ec242b6f

**New tests:**

| test | covers | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `processing/test_opencua.py::test_processor_override_matches_image_sizing` | flat, `size`, `images_kwargs`, and scoped `return_tensors`; each at init and per request | 8 failed (`assert 2691 == 312`) | passed |
| `processing/test_opencua.py::test_default_pixels_match_hf_processor` | default pixels equal HF `Qwen2VLImageProcessor` output | passed | passed (fails with the routing change alone: 99.6% of elements differ) |
| `generation/test_opencua.py::test_engine_applies_max_pixels` | `LLM` with `max_pixels`, dummy weights: 312 image tokens and device normalization off | failed (`assert not True`) | passed |

The processing tests run in the CPU "Multimodal Processor" step; they pass on CPU with transformers 5.20.2 and 5.23.0, and on the L4 wheel. The generation test needs CUDA and is marked `core_model`, so CI runs it in "Multimodal Models (Standard) 4"; it passes on the L4. `test_common.py -k opencua` and `test_tensor_schema.py::test_model_tensor_schema[xlangai/OpenCUA-7B]` pass on main and on this PR.

## Details

- **Root cause.** The processor is vendored because the checkpoint's remote code doesn't work with Transformers v5, and its `__call__` sends `**kwargs` only to the tokenizer. The tokenizer call is unchanged in this PR. `return_tensors` is resolved into the image kwargs once, so a scoped `images_kwargs.return_tensors` doesn't collide with it.
- **Why turn the flag off rather than wire `input_norm` into `OpenCUAVisionTransformer`.** Turning it off keeps the current numerics; that is how the default outputs above come out identical. Turning on device normalization for OpenCUA is a separate change that needs its own accuracy check. bee, colqwen3 and lightonocr opt out the same way, and the device-normalization table in `docs/design/mm_processing.md` already leaves OpenCUA out. Before this PR, `--mm-device-do-normalize` had no effect for OpenCUA. Now it logs that the model doesn't support it.
- **Other models.** I checked all 41 registered architectures that set `supports_mm_device_do_normalize`. OpenCUA is the only one that builds its own vision tower without `input_norm`.
- **Known limits, shared with Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL on main.** These are not changed here; OpenCUA now matches them (`5_kwargs_cases.tsv` in the gist):
  - A configured `max_pixels` plus a request `size.longest_edge` processes with the configured value (312 tokens), while sizing uses the request's value (72).
  - A `size` with only one edge fails in the HF image processor, which requires both.
  - With `max_pixels` and an image-size hint, the profiling dummy is smaller than a real image of the hinted size (540x960: 38 vs 312 tokens).

## Overview

Replace the six remaining raw `ValueError` sites in

failure is input validation or invalid object state. This is a file-level
Step 5 slice of #48227.

Part of #48227.

the review update: this is the only open PR referencing #48227, and the area
search found no other PR modifying these error sites.

  passed to the `LLM` constructor.
- Classify calls to `LLM.generate()`, `LLM.enqueue()`, `LLM.chat()`, and
  `LLM.enqueue_chat()` on non-generative runners as `RuntimeError` because
  they are capability checks on an initialized `LLM`, not validation of the
  method's input parameters.

  validation errors. The raw KV transfer dictionary is deliberately omitted

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Store the chunks that fit when a request exceeds the CPU tier
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #66696. A request with more unstored chunks than the CPU offload tier can hold was never offloaded: the whole store was rejected and retried unchanged on every step. The CPU manager now stores the chunks that fit, lowest token positions first, and reports the keys it had no room for; the scheduler offers those again on later steps.

## Claims

- A request whose unstored chunks exceed the CPU tier's free and evictable chunks is stored incrementally instead of not at all.
- Such a request no longer logs `cannot store chunks` and counts an allocation failure on every step.
- Stores that already fit are handled exactly as before.

## Validation

**End to end** (1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, `Qwen3-0.6B`, 64-token blocks). One `/v1/completions` request with a 7,663-token prompt (119 chunks), `max_tokens=400`, `temperature=0`. The CPU tier holds 13 chunks and cascades to an `fs` secondary tier:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 20000 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec",
      "cpu_bytes_to_use":100000000,
      "secondary_tiers":[{"type":"fs","root_dir":"<dir>"}]}}'
```

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `cannot store chunks` warnings | 401 | 0 |
| `vllm:kv_offload_allocation_failure_total` | 401 | 0 |
| store transfers (`vllm:kv_offload_store_size_count`) | 0 | 10 |
| `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_allocation_size` (count / sum) | 401 / 47,719 | 10 / 119 |
| chunks in the fs tier | 0 | 119 (873 MB) |

- The "this PR" column, and the two checks below, were re-run on the current revision (manager-side trimming). The `main` column is from an earlier `main`, before #64286.
- **Stored data is unchanged.** The same request against a 2 GB CPU tier (one store of 119 chunks, no trimming; run on an earlier revision of this PR) writes 120 files to the fs tier that are byte-identical (`sha256sum`) to the 120 files written through the ten trimmed stores.
- **The stored chunks load.** Restarting with a 2 GB CPU tier on the fs directory written by the small-tier run serves the prompt with `cached_tokens: 7616` and loads all 873 MB. The answer is correct. The 400-token greedy continuation matches the fresh run for about 90 tokens and then diverges inside a repetition loop; the fresh runs match exactly, so I attribute this to loaded-versus-fresh numerics rather than to this change, given the byte-identical files.

The issue reporter also [runs their own fix for the same failure in production](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/66696#issuecomment-6759047098) (not this branch) on 4x GB10 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash NVFP4 and reports about 40k warnings a day before and none after.

**Tests.**

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_offload -q
# 10 failed, 1827 passed, 6 skipped (merged with current main)
```

- The 10 failures are environmental. Six are `test_scheduler.py::test_dcp_partial_tail_*`, which need 2 GPUs (`World size (2) is larger than the number of available GPUs (1)`). Two are `test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e.py::test_inference_reuses_a_finished_kv_request_id` and `::test_inference_uses_completion_buffered_after_disconnect` (`AssertionError: no initial P2P fetch`), which failed the same way on unmodified `main` on this machine. Two are `test_fs_tier.py::test_store_reports_only_newly_written_blocks[True]` and `test_tiering_offloading.py::test_cascade_store_feeds_backpressure_only_written_bytes` (`transfer_bytes=None`), from #63524, which changed `csrc/fs_io.cpp`; the precompiled `fs_io_C` here predates it.
- `test_store_beyond_manager_capacity_continues_on_later_steps` (six full blocks, a manager that stores two keys per step and none on one step) stores all six blocks without an allocation failure. It and the finished-request test fail with the `ON_COMPUTE` handler from `main`.
- `test_cpu_manager_stores_the_leading_keys_that_fit`, `test_cpu_manager_trims_a_store_by_key_position` (two groups stay aligned), `test_partial_primary_store_cascades_each_resident_key_once` (fails on the previous revision), `test_chunks_left_unstored_by_a_finished_request_are_reported` and `test_partially_stored_handoff_is_reported` cover the manager, the tiering pass-through through a retry and the two cases that count as a loss.
- Nine existing tests in `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py` asserted that `prepare_store()` returns `None` when the tier is out of room. They now assert the trimmed result.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

## Details

**Root cause.** The `ON_COMPUTE` store handler passes every not-yet-stored chunk of a request to `manager.prepare_store()` in one call. `CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_store()` returned `None` when the new chunks exceed its free plus evictable chunks, and the handler then skips the store without advancing `next_stored_chunk_idx`, so the same oversized offer is made again on the next step.

**Fix.** Following the review, the manager trims the offer; the connector does not see its capacity.

- `PrepareStoreOutput.keys_to_retry` lists the offered keys to offer again because the manager had no room. Within a group they are the offered keys from the first one that did not fit on, by token position, including keys that are already resident, and they are disjoint from `keys_to_store`. It is empty by default, so other managers are unaffected. `OnComputeStoreHandler` asserts the constraints.
- `CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_store()` ranks the new keys by `req_context.get_offload_key_position()`, stores the lowest positions that fit, and reports as keys to retry every offered key of a group from its first key that did not fit on, resident keys included, since the connector offers all of them again. `keys_to_store` and the store spec stay in offer order, so they still line up with the GPU blocks group by group, and a trimmed store covers the same tokens in every group. Offered chunks that are already resident do not count as room, because they are protected from eviction. `prepare_write()` (secondary-to-primary promotions) keeps the all-or-nothing behaviour.
- `TieringOffloadingManager.prepare_store()` passes the result through and does not cascade keys to retry to request-level tiers as existing chunks, so a resident key after the cut is cascaded once, when it is offered again.
- `OnComputeStoreHandler` ends each group's store range at its first chunk to retry, so the cursor only passes the chunks the manager took and the rest is offered on the next step. While the request runs, an offer of which nothing is stored is not a failure.
- A finished request or a hand-off with keys to retry is not offered again, so it counts as an allocation failure (`StoreJobSink.record_allocation_failure()`).
- `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_allocation_size` records the size after the trim.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- `CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_store()` no longer rejects an offer that does not fit; callers that relied on `None` for that case get a trimmed result instead. In-tree it is called by the store handlers, directly or through the tiering manager.
- A request that finishes before all its chunks were consumed stores only the leading part, since a finished request gets a single store attempt.
- Without a secondary tier, an oversized request now cycles through the CPU tier and evicts older chunks, including its own prefix. Requests that grow over several steps already behave this way (#67287).
- `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_allocation_size` no longer records a sample for an offer of which nothing fits.

**Duplicate check.** No other PR references #66696. #66154 (draft) addresses the same failure with opt-in bounded PUT staging (`put_batch_chunks`, `put_max_inflight_chunks`, `put_get_reserve_chunks`) and leaves the default path unchanged, so the issue still reproduces by default with it. This PR is a small default-on fix with no new config; the difference is [explained in the issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/66696#issuecomment-6758991874), and the reporter asked for it to go ahead. Unlike #66154 it does not offer a finished request's remaining chunks in its final pass. Happy to fold it into #66154 if maintainers prefer. #62931 / #62932 cover the load-side counterpart.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview The parser passes NumPy images through as arrays and keeps PIL frames as a list inside a `(frames, metadata)` video, but Muse Spark Open's own preprocessing reads `.mode` on every image and `.shape` on every frame, so both inputs fail with `AttributeError`. This PR converts images with `to_pil_image`, as #68655 did for vLLM's own HF processors, and converts PIL frames with the existing `_to_rgb` before stacking them into an array. ## Claims - NumPy images (HWC or CHW, uint8 or float in [0, 1]) and CPU tensor images give the same pixel values and token count as the same image passed as PIL. - `(frames, metadata)` videos made of RGB, grayscale or RGBA PIL frames give the same output as the same frames converted to RGB and passed as an array. - PIL images and array videos take the same path as before. ## Validation Everything ran on CPU on an RTX 4090 machine, using the precompiled wheel for `efffc2a0bc`. For the base runs I copied `processor.py` from base `a25064c85d` over the wheel, and for the PR runs I copied it from PR commit `7657c1185e`. `processor.py` is identical between `efffc2a0bc` and the base. The first revision of this PR added `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_muse_spark.py`, which called the preprocessing functions directly. One test compared a NumPy image with the same image as PIL. The other compared a `(PIL frames, metadata)` video with the same frames converted to RGB and stacked into an array, for RGB, L and RGBA frames. I removed it to match #68655 and #69052; the results below are from that revision. Base: ```text tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_muse_spark.py::test_preprocess_numpy_image_matches_pil FAILED [ 25%] tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_muse_spark.py::test_preprocess_pil_frame_video_matches_numpy[RGB] FAILED [ 50%] tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_muse_spark.py::test_preprocess_pil_frame_video_matches_numpy[L] FAILED [ 75%] tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_muse_spark.py::test_preprocess_pil_frame_video_matches_numpy[RGBA] FAILED [100%] E AttributeError: 'numpy.ndarray' object has no attribute 'mode' E AttributeError: 'Image' object has no attribute 'shape'. Did you mean: 'save'? ========================= 4 failed, 1 warning in 2.72s ========================= ``` PR: ```text tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_muse_spark.py::test_preprocess_numpy_image_matches_pil PASSED [ 25%] tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_muse_spark.py::test_preprocess_pil_frame_video_matches_numpy[RGB] PASSED [ 50%] tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_muse_spark.py::test_preprocess_pil_frame_video_matches_numpy[L] PASSED [ 75%] tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_muse_spark.py::test_preprocess_pil_frame_video_matches_numpy[RGBA] PASSED [100%] ========================= 4 passed, 1 warning in 2.58s ========================= ``` I also ran the full multimodal processor with the config and tokenizer of `meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4`. This needs no weights, so it ran on CPU. Base: ```text RESULT image: PIL: OK placeholder_tokens=66 prompt_len=76 RESULT image: np.ndarray: AttributeError: 'numpy.ndarray' object has no attribute 'mode' RESULT video: (np.ndarray, metadata): OK placeholder_tokens=289 prompt_len=299 RESULT video: (list of PIL frames, metadata): AttributeError: 'Image' object has no attribute 'shape' RESULT video: (list of grayscale PIL frames, metadata): AttributeError: 'Image' object has no attribute 'shape' ``` PR: ```text RESULT image: PIL: OK placeholder_tokens=66 prompt_len=76 RESULT image: np.ndarray: OK placeholder_tokens=66 prompt_len=76 RESULT video: (np.ndarray, metadata): OK placeholder_tokens=289 prompt_len=299 RESULT video: (list of PIL frames, metadata): OK placeholder_tokens=289 prompt_len=299 RESULT video: (list of grayscale PIL frames, metadata): OK placeholder_tokens=289 prompt_len=299 ```
Reproducer (python repro.py) ```python """Muse Spark Open: numpy images and (PIL frames, metadata) videos through the processor.""" import sys import traceback import numpy as np from PIL import Image from vllm.config import ModelConfig from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY MODEL = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4" def main(): cfg = ModelConfig(MODEL, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1, "video": 1, "audio": 0}, mm_processor_cache_gb=0) proc = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(cfg) rng = np.random.default_rng(0) arr = rng.integers(0, 256, (224, 224, 3), dtype=np.uint8) frames = rng.integers(0, 256, (8, 224, 224, 3), dtype=np.uint8) meta = {"fps": 2.0, "frames_indices": list(range(8)), "total_num_frames": 8} cases = { "image: PIL": ("image", Image.fromarray(arr)), "image: np.ndarray": ("image", arr), "video: (np.ndarray, metadata)": ("video", (frames, meta)), "video: (list of PIL frames, metadata)": ("video", ([Image.fromarray(f) for f in frames], meta)), "video: (list of grayscale PIL frames, metadata)": ("video", ([Image.fromarray(f).convert("L") for f in frames], meta)), } for name, (modality, data) in cases.items(): prompt = f"Question: {proc.info.get_placeholder(modality)} what's in the media? Answer:" try: out = proc(prompt, mm_items=proc.info.parse_mm_data({modality: data}), hf_processor_mm_kwargs={}) n = sum(p.length for p in out["mm_placeholders"][modality]) print(f"RESULT {name}: OK placeholder_tokens={n} prompt_len={len(out['prompt_token_ids'])}") except Exception as e: c = e.__cause__ or e print(f"RESULT {name}: {type(c).__name__}: {str(c).splitlines()[0][:150]}") tb = traceback.extract_tb(c.__traceback__)[-1] print(f" at {tb.filename.split('site-packages/')[-1]}:{tb.lineno} {tb.line}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
The model has 816B parameters, so I couldn't run it end to end. ## Details `MuseSparkOmniMultiModalProcessor` runs its own preprocessing instead of an HF processor, and it assumes PIL images and array frames. The parser doesn't guarantee either: - NumPy images stay arrays. #68655 fixed the same problem in the processors under `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/`, but Muse Spark wasn't one of them. - The processor sets `video_needs_metadata=True`, so a video has to be a `(frames, metadata)` tuple, and the parser returns the tuple unchanged. A list of PIL frames therefore reaches `preprocess_video` as a list. Notes on the change: - `to_pil_image` returns PIL images unchanged. It doesn't accept 2D or 4-channel arrays. Those raised `AttributeError` before and now raise `ValueError`, the same as the processors changed in #68655. - PIL frames go through `_to_rgb`, the same helper used for images, so grayscale frames become RGB and RGBA frames are composited over white. Without it, grayscale frames stack into a 3D array and fail later in `permute`. #69089, merged after this branch's base, makes the parser convert PIL frames to RGB, so on current main `_to_rgb` gets RGB frames from the parser and returns them unchanged. It still covers direct callers of these functions. - Online requests are unaffected: images reach the processor as PIL, and decoded videos arrive as arrays. - A CUDA tensor video also fails here, at `np.asarray(frames)` in `preprocess_video`. My open PR #69052 handles tensor videos in three other processors with `.cpu().numpy()`, so I left this case out until that approach is reviewed. I didn't find an issue or PR where someone reported or is working on this. Open PRs #68740 and #68886 change other parts of `processor.py`. I used Claude to help find this bug, reproduce it, and draft this description. I worked out the design with Claude, which also made the edits at my request; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and commands above. ---

commits.pr_title: [CI] Decouple LoRA layer tests from GLM model imports
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Fix XPU collection failures in `tests/lora/test_layers.py` without moving
`_Glm5NextMergedColumnParallelLinear` or skipping tests.

The top-level GLM import triggers the package's XPU restriction before
pytest can collect unrelated LoRA tests. Replace that dependency with a
test-local `MergedColumnParallelLinear` subclass providing replicated-shard
metadata and output sizes.

This test checks LoRA B-matrix sharding, not GLM's base-weight loaders.
Existing parameter combinations and assertions remain unchanged.
No production code changes are required.

## Overview

Three decode-time improvements to Inkling2's SM12x low-M (M <= 16) BF16 GEMM from #69028 (`ops/gemv.py`, now `ops/ll_gemm_sm120.py` as `sm12x_bf16_ll_gemm`):

1. **Split-K for narrow outputs.** When there are too few column tiles to fill the GPU, the kernel splits K, deterministically. The short-conv projection (N=32) now uses it instead of `F.linear`: **up to 7.1×** faster.
2. **Batched GEMM for the loop blend.** A 3D weight runs a batched matmul, replacing the blend's two `torch.bmm` calls: **up to 5.1×** faster.
3. **Fused q/k/v projection.** `qkv_bmm` computes q, k and v, each from its own input, in one launch instead of three: **1.2×** faster.

End to end on RTX 5090, decode steps are **6.5–7.5% faster** (`vllm bench serve`, DSpark). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

## Claims

- Shapes that don't split (`linear()`, LM head) match main's `_gemv` bitwise and within 0.1 µs.
- Split-K is deterministic: the last CTA reduces the partials in split order.
- **Not tuned or validated on DGX Spark (SM121).** The dispatch covers SM121.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/models/inkling2/test_core_ops.py
# 81 passed in 51.40s (RTX 5090, f438656f4b)
```

**Kernel** (RTX 5090, SM120; CUPTI, CUDA graph over rotating weight copies > 3× L2; median of 3 interleaved rounds with alternating order):

| Op | M | main | this PR | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| q/k/v, 8608×2304 | 1 | 30.6 µs (1.30 TB/s) | 25.8 µs (1.54 TB/s) | 1.19× |
| | 8 | 31.4 µs (1.27 TB/s) | 25.9 µs (1.54 TB/s) | 1.21× |
| | 16 | 31.3 µs (1.28 TB/s) | 26.3 µs (1.53 TB/s) | 1.19× |
| Loop blend, 3 streams | 1 | 6.9 µs (0.53 TB/s) | 5.2 µs (0.69 TB/s) | 1.31× |
| | 8 | 27.6 µs (0.15 TB/s) | 5.4 µs (0.78 TB/s) | **5.11×** |
| | 16 | 28.0 µs (0.17 TB/s) | 5.7 µs (0.86 TB/s) | **4.93×** |
| Loop blend, 1 stream | 1 | 5.7 µs (0.21 TB/s) | 3.9 µs (0.31 TB/s) | 1.46× |

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build][NVIDIA] Use PyTorch's cu135 nightly for Rubin and document the ptxas 13.5.37 SM107 workaround
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Two changes to the Rubin prerelease images:

1. **cu135 PyTorch.** Since #65765, the Rubin images use CUDA 13.5 but kept PyTorch's cu134 nightly and the `cuda13.4` builders, because PyTorch had published neither for 13.5. PyTorch now publishes cu135 torch nightlies (since 2026-11-13) and `cuda13.5` manylinux builders, so the Rubin build moves to both.
2. **Wrong results on SM107.** [Reported on the vLLM Slack](https://vllm-dev.slack.com/archives/C0AQPDP5ETX/p1794875112321329): in the current `cu135-nightly` images, ptxas 13.5.37 (CUDA 13.5.0) silently miscompiles some Triton kernels for `sm_107a` (VR200, R100), which turns GLM-5.3's output into gibberish. Rubin images now install the Triton wheel that the cu135 torch nightly requires (`triton==3.9.0+gitb7ddcf86`, the Triton 3.9.0 release) from PyTorch's index instead of building Triton from source. The Rubin build docs now warn about ptxas 13.5.37 and give a `docker run` option that keeps Triton on the ptxas-blackwell 13.4 this wheel bundles. The images themselves don't change which ptxas Triton uses. This also removes the PyTorch/Triton requirement conflict reported in #64761.

## Claims

- `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt` pins `torch==2.16.0.dev20261116+cu135` from the cu135 nightly index. torch's CUDA runtime wheels move to 13.5 with it (`cuda-toolkit` 13.4.1 → 13.5.0, `nvidia-cuda-runtime` 13.4.49 → 13.5.37).
- PyTorch publishes no cu135 torchvision or torchaudio yet. They use the cu134 nightlies of the same date (`torchvision 0.30.0.dev20261116+cu134`, `torchaudio 2.11.0.dev20261116+cu134`), from a second extra index.
- The two Rubin release jobs and the guide's build commands use `pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda13.5` and `pytorch/manylinuxaarch64-builder:cuda13.5`.
- Rubin images install Triton as the `triton==3.9.0+gitb7ddcf86` wheel from PyTorch's nightly index, which torch's own requirement pulls in. The Triton source build, its two scripts and its build arguments are removed; only the two Rubin release jobs used them. `uv pip check` passes in this PR's image; in the current nightly it reports `torch requires triton==3.9.0+gitfc8d31a5, but 3.8.0+git3f6e4113 is installed`, among others.
- The Rubin build docs warn that ptxas 13.5.37 silently miscompiles some `sm_107a` code. They give `--env TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.14/dist-packages/triton/backends/nvidia/bin/ptxas-blackwell`, the `ptxas-blackwell` that this wheel bundles (13.4.59). Triton 3.9 uses it for every SM90-and-newer kernel. Without the option, importing FlashInfer points Triton at the ptxas on `PATH`, which is 13.5.37. No image sets the variable, and the Dockerfile has no Rubin-specific stages.
- On VR200, with vLLM and FlashInfer imported first as a server does, the Slack reproducer and vLLM's torch.compile'd `per_block_cast_to_fp8` give wrong results in the current nightly and in this PR's image as built. With the documented option, they give correct results in this PR's image.
- On VR200, round 3's image of this PR (same Triton wheel, variable set in the image) served MiniMax-M3.1-Flash with the same request results and comparable GSM8K accuracy as the current `cu135-nightly` image. This head's image, with the documented option, serves Qwen3-0.6B correctly.

## Validation

**Setup (rounds 1 to 3).** One VR200 node: 4 GPUs (SM107), aarch64, host driver 620.43. That is a native R620 driver, so the image's forward-compatibility driver isn't loaded. NVIDIA Container Toolkit 1.18.0. The baseline is `vllm/vllm-openai:cu135-nightly-60bd6dd2edd175a1c55fd3488f871e4c3d2ef27d` (`sha256:4c2a5b41718b…`), main at this PR's original base.

### Round 4: the ptxas option, documented (this head)

Review asked to avoid the Rubin-only Dockerfile stages. This head drops them and the build-time check. Instead, the Rubin build docs warn about ptxas 13.5.37 and give `--env TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.14/dist-packages/triton/backends/nvidia/bin/ptxas-blackwell`.

**Setup.**
- The image was built from 8b40eab915 with the guide's ARM64 command, plus round 3's `--add-host` workaround. This head includes a merge of main that moved the default Python to 3.14.
- It ran on one VR200 system: 2 GPUs (SM107), aarch64, host driver 620.62.
- Each check ran in a fresh container, once as the image starts by default and once with the documented option.

| Check | This PR's image, as built | With the documented `--env` |

| Triton's SM107 ptxas after `import vllm, flashinfer` | `/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas`, 13.5.37, set by FlashInfer | the wheel's `ptxas-blackwell`, 13.4.59 |
| Slack reproducer, after importing vLLM and FlashInfer. Wrong outputs, of 98,304 | 81,920 | 0 |
| `per_block_cast_to_fp8`, torch.compile'd vs eager, fp32 input, after importing vLLM and FlashInfer. Rows of the last partial 128-row block with differing FP8 values, at 2624×6144, 576×6144, 192×6144 and 320×6144 | 64 at each shape | 0 at each shape |
| `uv pip check` | All 245 packages compatible | All 245 packages compatible |

- **Documented path:** it exists in the image, which runs Python 3.14.10.
- **Real server:** with the option, `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` in the default compiled mode starts and answers two requests correctly, with no errors in its log.
- **The option reaches the engine:** I pointed the variable at a wrapper that logs its callers and then runs the documented `ptxas-blackwell`. All 48 calls came from the engine process (46 assemblies, 2 version queries).
- **Longer cast check:** 10 shapes, bf16 and fp32, with the option. It shows the same isolated single-value differences as round 3, at the same rows: compiled-vs-eager rounding, with no garbled blocks.

"""ptxas 13.5.37 sm_107a miscompile: FP32 indexed multiplication.

No vLLM, torch.compile, FP8, reductions, logarithms, or exponentials.
Run in a fresh process/cache with each ptxas version. --safe-ceil and
--block=128 are controls that should pass with either assembler. """

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl
from triton.backends.compiler import GPUTarget
from triton.compiler import ASTSource


@triton.jit
def floor_div(a, b):
    # Triton integer division truncates; floor needs a correction for unlike signs.
    q = a // b
    r = a % b
    fixed = tl.where(r != 0, q - 1, q)
    return tl.where((a < 0) != (b < 0), fixed, q)


@triton.jit
def indexed_multiply(
    X, A, Y, m, n, bm, bn, ns, count, SAFE: tl.constexpr, B: tl.constexpr
):
    i = tl.program_id(0) * B + tl.arange(0, B)
    row = i.to(tl.int64) // n
    col = i.to(tl.int64) % n
    # Ceiling block counts: the bad sign test makes nc=1 instead of 2.
    nr = -floor_div(m, -bm)
    nc = -floor_div(n, -bn)
    if SAFE:
        # Equivalent for positive dimensions; avoids the miscompiled negation.
        nr = (m + bm - 1) // bm
        nc = (n + bn - 1) // bn
    # Retain the original padding-related indexing that triggers the optimizer bug.
    xi = (row % (bm * nr)) * n + col % (bn * nc)
    ai = nc * ((row // bm) % nr) + (col // bn) % ns
    x = tl.load(X + xi, i < count, other=0)
    a = tl.load(A + ai, i < count, other=0)
    tl.store(Y + i, x * a, i < count)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--safe-ceil", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--block", type=int, default=256)
    parser.add_argument("--save", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    m, n, bm, bn = 512, 192, 128, 128
    i = torch.arange(m * n, device="cuda")
    x = (i % 256 + 1).float()
    a = torch.arange(1, 9, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
    y = torch.empty_like(x)
    ref = x * a[(i // n // bm) * 2 + i % n // bn]
    # Keep the same i64 scalar ABI as the original Inductor-generated kernel.
    signature = dict(zip(indexed_multiply.arg_names[:9], ["*fp32"] * 3 + ["i64"] * 6))
    kernel = triton.compile(
        ASTSource(
            indexed_multiply,
            signature=signature,
            constexprs={"SAFE": args.safe_ceil, "B": args.block},
        ),
        target=GPUTarget("cuda", 107, 32),
        # 128 threads: block=256 gives two elements per thread; block=128 gives one.
        options={"num_warps": 4},
    )
    kernel[(triton.cdiv(m * n, args.block), 1, 1)](
        x,
        a,
        y,
        m,
        n,
        bm,
        bn,
        2,
        m * n,
    )
    bad = y != ref
    count = bad.sum().item()
    print(f"block={args.block} safe_ceil={args.safe_ceil} mismatches={count}/{m * n}")
    if count:
        idx = bad.nonzero()[:8, 0]
        print("indices:", idx.tolist())
        print("actual:", y[idx].tolist())
        print("expected:", ref[idx].tolist())
    if args.save:
        args.save.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for ext in ("ptx", "ttir", "ttgir", "llir"):
            (args.save / f"kernel.{ext}").write_text(kernel.asm[ext])
        (args.save / "kernel.cubin").write_bytes(kernel.asm["cubin"])
    raise SystemExit(bool(count))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

In the round 1 image, with lmcache 0.5.7.post1 installed with `--no-deps`, that import succeeds against torch `2.16.0.dev20261116+cu135`. It also succeeds in the baseline nightly, which already ships 0.5.7.post1.

## Details

- **Root cause.** ptxas 13.5.37's optimizer miscompiles a negated floor-division ceiling, `-floor_div(n, -bn)`, in i64 index math when each thread handles two elements. Inductor lowers ceil-div this way, so torch.compile'd code hits it. In the reproducer, the column-block count comes out as 1 instead of 2. In `per_block_cast_to_fp8`, the last partial 128-row block of a weight whose row count isn't a multiple of 128 reads the wrong rows, with fp32 input. ptxas 13.4.92, `DISABLE_PTXAS_OPT=1`, or writing the ceiling as `(n + bn - 1) // bn` avoid it. The current images hit it because Triton 3.8's bundled ptxas-blackwell (13.3) can't assemble SM107, so the Rubin build pointed Triton at the image's own ptxas, which is 13.5.37 in the CUDA 13.5 images.
- **Why the wheel's ptxas, as a documented option.** The Triton 3.9.0 wheel bundles ptxas-blackwell 13.4.59, which assembles the reproducer correctly (round 2). FlashInfer 0.7.4's `flashinfer/triton/__init__.py` sets `TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH` to `shutil.which("ptxas")` when the variable is unset and that ptxas is release 13 or newer, and a plain `import flashinfer` runs it. Setting the variable when the container starts keeps Triton on the wheel's ptxas.
  - The previous revision (42833f4230) set it in Rubin images through two extra Dockerfile stages. One `ENV` for all images doesn't work: Docker defines the variable even when its value is empty, and Triton 3.8 (in the other images) then raises `PermissionError` for Blackwell GPUs, because it tries to run `""` as the ptxas.
  - NVIDIA is expected to ship a fixed ptxas, so this PR documents the option rather than baking a workaround into the images.
  - Triton `main` already bundles only ptxas 13.5.37 (`cmake/nvidia-toolchain-version.json`), so the option stops helping after a torch bump that brings such a Triton. `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt` says to check this before a bump.
- **Scope.** Triton 3.9 uses `ptxas-blackwell` for all of SM90 and newer, so with the documented option, ptxas 13.4.59 assembles every Triton kernel on Hopper, Blackwell and Rubin GPUs in Rubin images.
- **Other code that ptxas 13.5.37 assembles.** The documented option covers the Triton path only, and the bug looks specific to `sm_107a`. The reproducer's PTX, assembled by hand for `sm_100f` with ptxas 13.5.37, runs correctly on VR200; for `sm_107a`, the same PTX gives the 81,920 wrong outputs.
  - vLLM's own CUDA kernels are built for SM100-family targets (the Rubin arch list has 10.0, not 10.7), so this trigger doesn't seem to reach them.
  - DeepEP's `sm_107a` kernels are assembled by the builder's ptxas, 13.5.37 with the `cuda13.5` builders.
  - Code that FlashInfer and vLLM JIT-compile at runtime is assembled by the image's own ptxas 13.5.37, whichever builder is used. In the MiniMax run above, that was `-gencode=arch=compute_107a,code=sm_107a` for FlashInfer's `trtllm_comm` and vLLM's MiniMax attention kernels. The current nightly does the same.
  - None of these showed wrong results here. A corrected ptxas from NVIDIA is the complete fix.
- **Triton 3.9 for vLLM.** MiniMax-M3's sparse prefill kernel for Hopper still uses block pointers, which Triton 3.9 removed. On SM90, it won't compile in this image until #66099 lands. Rubin GPUs don't use it. Triton 3.9 also warns once per process that `TRITON_DEFAULT_FP_FUSION` is unset; its default, fusion enabled, is unchanged.
- **#64761 and #64813.** #64761 reports the PyTorch/Triton requirement conflict in these images. This PR removes it for the Rubin images, since the image's Triton is now the wheel torch requires. #64813 (open) keeps a source-built Triton through later uv installs. This PR removes the source build, so #64813 would no longer apply.
- **Why this isn't a duplicate.** No open or closed PR moves the Rubin torch pins to cu135, or works around ptxas 13.5.37.
  - I searched PR titles and bodies for `rubin-prerelease`, `cu135`, `torch cu135`, `rubin torch`, `CUDA 13.5 torch`, `ptxas`, `13.5.37`, `sm_107a`, `triton 3.9`, `rubin triton`, `TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH` and `flashinfer ptxas`. Searched again on 2026-11-19, after this revision.
  - I checked the changed files of every PR created since 2026-11-12. For open PRs updated since 2026-11-13, I checked 1,000 of the 1,174; that's the most GitHub's search returns.
  - #67371 mentions cu135, but it bumps lmcache and doesn't touch these files.
  - #32704 auto-configures `TRITON_PTXAS_PATH` for new GPU architectures, not for this bug.
  - #68088 (open) restructures the same Dockerfile for build caching. It doesn't touch Triton or its ptxas, but both PRs edit the Dockerfile, `docker/versions.json` and the stage graph, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- **torchvision and torchaudio stay on cu134.** PyTorch's nightlies of both are now `py3-none` wheels. They require only `torch>=2.14` (torchvision) and `torch>=2.11` (torchaudio), so the cu135 torch satisfies them. Their CUDA 13.4 kernels run on the 13.5 runtime through CUDA minor-version compatibility, as all three packages did before this PR. Once PyTorch publishes cu135 builds, the second index and the `+cu134` pins can go.
- **Builder tags.** The `cuda13.5` builder tags float, as the `cuda13.4` ones did. The other release jobs pin a commit-suffixed builder tag.
- **`VLLM_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY_PATH`.** #65765 set it because vLLM's default compat path follows torch's CUDA version (`/usr/local/cuda-13.4/compat`), and a 13.5 image doesn't have that path. With cu135 torch, the default path (`/usr/local/cuda-13.5/compat`) exists too. The `ENV` stays as an explicit setting; only its comment loses the cu134 example.
- **Dockerfile graph.** Removing the Triton source build drops its edge from `extensions-build` to `vllm-openai-base`, so the `update-dockerfile-graph` hook's regenerated PNG is included.
- **R610 hosts.** On a VR200 host with an R610 driver (610.47), where the image's 620.70 forward-compatibility driver loads, both images fail the same way. They hit a CUDA illegal memory access during the FlashInfer autotune warmup, before serving. The baseline nightly fails too, so the cause predates this PR, and the guide already asks for R620 or newer.
- **CI coverage.** The Rubin steps run only in nightly release builds (`NIGHTLY=1`), so PR CI doesn't exercise them. No x86_64 image was built, because I had no x86 Rubin host where I could run Docker builds. For x86_64, only the dependency resolution above is checked; PyTorch's index has the same Triton wheel for x86_64.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview Fix Whisper prompt conditioning (the OpenAI `prompt` field on `/v1/audio/transcriptions`). FIX #53206 `get_generation_prompt()` prefixed the prompt with `<|prev|>`, which is not a Whisper token, and the renderer then prepended `<|startoftranscript|>` in front of it. The decoder now gets the reference layout: ``` main: <|startoftranscript|> < | pre v | > prompt <|startoftranscript|><|lang|><|task|><|notimestamps|> this PR: <|startofprev|> ␣prompt <|startoftranscript|><|lang|><|task|><|notimestamps|> ``` Also explains #35276 (same symptom, closed as stale) and unblocks the standard-prompt half of #34518. #44662 and #54072 touch the same line. ## Claims - A transcription request with `prompt` reaches the decoder as `get_prompt_ids(prompt)` followed by the SOT sequence, token for token the same as HF transformers and openai-whisper. - Requests without `prompt` produce the same decoder input as on main. - Every other Whisper decoder prompt (explicit or implicit, including an empty one) still gets `<|startoftranscript|>` prepended when it lacks it, as on main. Canary and Cohere ASR are unchanged. ## Validation **Renderer tests (CPU).** `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_whisper.py`, through both `render_cmpl` (offline) and `render_cmpl_async` (the transcription path): ```bash pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_whisper.py -k decoder ``` | | main `9c1d45c218` | before review fix `ca45b48a9a` | this PR `890decd022` | |---|---|---|---| | empty / SOT-less decoder prompt (`test_decoder_start_token`) | pass | **6 failed** | pass | | prompted request (`test_generation_prompt_decoder_layout`) | **2 failed** | pass | pass |
Raw output (Apple M4, VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu) main `9c1d45c218`: ``` E AssertionError: assert [50258, 27, 9..., 85, 91, ...] == [50362, 2425,...291, 322, ...] 2 failed, 8 passed, 3 deselected, 2 warnings in 20.05s ``` before review fix `ca45b48a9a`: ``` E assert [] == [50258] E AssertionError: assert [50259, 50360, 50364] == [50258, 50259, 50360, 50364] 6 failed, 4 passed, 3 deselected, 2 warnings in 20.58s ``` this PR `890decd022`: ``` 10 passed, 3 deselected, 1 warning in 20.75s ```
**LLM-level test (GPU).** `test_decoder_prompt_layout` in `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper.py` sends a prompted request, an empty decoder prompt and an SOT-less decoder prompt through `LLM.generate` and checks their `prompt_token_ids`: ```bash VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper.py -m core_model -k test_decoder_prompt_layout ```
Raw output (NVIDIA GB10, vllm/vllm-openai:nightly 0.33.0rc1.dev1030+gcf5cea2da with this PR's changes applied) The PR's changes apply cleanly to `cf5cea2da`. `gpu_memory_utilization` was capped at 0.1 by a local plugin because the machine is shared. before review fix `ca45b48a9a`: ``` vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py:614: in _validate_model_input > raise VLLMValidationError(f"The {prompt_type} prompt cannot be empty") E vllm.exceptions.VLLMValidationError: The decoder prompt cannot be empty 1 failed, 12 deselected, 9 warnings in 253.45s (0:04:13) ``` this PR `890decd022`: ``` tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper.py::test_decoder_prompt_layout[openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo] PASSED 1 passed, 12 deselected, 9 warnings in 192.13s (0:03:12) ```
**Serving.** With the token rename alone (first commit), a served `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` on a 30 s Mandarin clip (`response_format=verbose_json`, `prompt=這是繁體中文的語音轉錄。`) went from 1 segment (`。`, everything before the final chunk lost) to 2 segments with the full transcript, and a 9 s English clip lost its hallucinated `"The reason"` prefix. Two independent reports confirm the full layout end to end: [`mary_had_lamb` ×4 on v0.27.1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53207#issuecomment-6221403091) (4 of 4 recitations with a prompt, 2 of 4 with the rename alone) and [a wake-word set in production](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53207#issuecomment-6771122904) (82/84/81 of 88 recognized, 48/51/59 before, faster-whisper 86/85/83). ## Details **Root cause.** 1. `<|prev|>` is in no Whisper vocabulary, so it tokenized into six text tokens (`'<', '|', 'pre', 'v', '|', '>'`). The prompt-conditioning token is `<|startofprev|>`: id 50362 in [whisper-large-v3-turbo](https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo/blob/main/tokenizer_config.json) and [whisper-large-v3](https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-large-v3/blob/main/tokenizer_config.json), 50361 in [whisper-small](https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-small/blob/main/tokenizer_config.json) and [whisper-large-v2](https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-large-v2/blob/main/tokenizer_config.json), `sot_prev` in [openai/whisper `tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/openai/whisper/blob/main/whisper/tokenizer.py). 2. `build_enc_dec_input` prepends the decoder start token to every decoder prompt that does not begin with it, so a prompted request still decoded from `<|startoftranscript|><|startofprev|>…`. HF transformers never prepends it to user-provided Whisper decoder ids ([`generation/utils.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.1.0/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L958-L959)). With the extra token some 30 s windows end after a few tokens and their text is silently dropped. **Fix.** - The prompt is encoded as `<|startofprev|> {prompt.strip()}`; the leading space and `strip()` make the token IDs equal to HF `get_prompt_ids(prompt)`. The example client's docs referenced `<|prev|>` and are updated. - `EncDecMultiModalProcessor.should_skip_decoder_start_token(decoder_prompt_token_ids)` decides per decoder prompt and defaults to the existing `skip_decoder_start_token` attribute; `build_enc_dec_input` accepts either that bool or a predicate. Whisper skips only when the prompt opens with `<|startofprev|>`, and keeps the default without a tokenizer (`skip_tokenizer_init=True`). - An earlier revision set `skip_decoder_start_token = True` on the Whisper processor, which also dropped the start token from empty and SOT-less decoder prompts ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53207#issuecomment-6968951940)). Deciding per prompt keeps those as on main. **CI.** The renderer tests run in "(CPU) Multimodal Processor", the LLM-level test in "Multimodal Models (Standard) 4: other + whisper" (`-m core_model`). **Not addressed here.** Prompts are not cut to the last 223 tokens as openai-whisper does, special-token text inside a prompt is still parsed as special tokens, and #55281 (fewer, longer `verbose_json` segments with a prompt) remains. With a working prompt, Whisper can echo it on silence, which is standard Whisper behavior. ---

## Overview

Adds Thinking Machines' [Inkling 2 Mini](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini) (`Inkling2LoopForConditionalGeneration`, `model_type: inkling2_loop`) and its variable-loop research checkpoint, [TML-d24-varloop-research](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research). Builds on the Inkling 2 Small support (#67325, #67880, #68761). The recipe is in #69027.

## Claims

- **Inkling 2 Mini serves end to end:** a 26B-total / 3.5B-active looped MoE. Its loop core (layers 6–17) runs three passes per token with shared weights. Every pass starts from the prelude's attention-residual state, keeps its own KV and conv-state caches, and from the second pass on merges gated messages from the previous pass's two blocks into each core sublayer input.
- **Variable-loop checkpoints:** `--hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"loop_num_passes": N, "loop_share_cache": true}}'` (rejected on fixed-loop checkpoints; DSpark requires the checkpoint's pass count).
- **DSpark speculative decoding** reading the target's hidden states at layer visits, text and image input, and the `inkling` reasoning and tool-call parsers (Python and Rust frontends).
- **Hardware:** Blackwell (SM100/SM103), Hopper (SM90) and DGX Spark (SM120/SM121).

## Validation

Re-run on this branch (eb7981b5f9, on current main), GB200:

- `pytest tests/models/inkling2/test_core_ops.py` 65 passed, 4 skipped; `test_attention.py` 147 passed; `test_model.py` 21 passed; `test_moe.py` 102 passed, 5 skipped.
- GSM8K (200 questions, temperature 0, DSpark): Inkling 2 Mini TP1 97.0% (mean acceptance length 3.58); Inkling 2 Small TP4 98.0% (4.43). The previous revision scored 97.5% / 99.0%; the differences are one and two questions.
- `vllm bench forward` at 51K context (TP1, DSpark): verify 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 requests 5.87 / 10.40 / 21.16 / 35.02 ms per step; an 8K-token prefill 116.2 ms. Against the previous revision on the same node: within 0.1% in every case.

Earlier validation on the pre-squash branch (GB200, TP1 unless noted, DSpark with 7 tokens and probabilistic drafting):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/models/inkling2` (core ops, attention, MoE, model, all-reduce, DSpark, vision, processing) | all pass |
| GSM8K, 1,319 questions, temperature 0 | 96.8% (96.7% without speculative decoding; 96.2% at TP2) |
| Needle-in-a-haystack, 4K–1M × 11 depths × 10 (TP4) | 550/550 |
| MMMU-Pro standard-10 / vision, first 150 (TP4) | 78.0% / 73.3% |
| HLE text-only, first 50 (TP4) | 20/47 scored |
| Default command (Rust frontend), GSM8K 200 | 97.5%, mean acceptance length 3.57 |
| TML-d24-varloop-research, 2 passes + shared KV cache | serves; chat/reasoning/image/tool smoke tests pass |
| Inkling 2 Small TP4 (shared kernels), GSM8K 200 | 98.0–99.0% |

Numerics follow the reference implementation (same data types, FP32 message merges; only the reduction order differs). On a fixed prompt, every layer visit's hidden state differs from the reference by about as much as the reference's own FlashAttention-4 and PyTorch attention paths differ from each other, and the MoE matches bitwise given the same inputs.

Performance (GB200, TP1, multi-turn agentic sessions with ~2K-token tool outputs, 1,024 output tokens, prefix caching): ~4,400 / 3,200 / 2,100 output tok/s per GPU at 100 tok/s per user with 32K / 64K / 128K-token sessions. Hopper and DGX Spark were validated separately.

## Details

- **Per-pass caches** are extra attention layers (`Inkling2AttentionPassCache`) and per-pass conv states, so the KV cache manager and prefix caching need no changes.
- **Loop driver** (`vllm/models/inkling2/nvidia/loop.py`): all four message reads of a layer run as one attention-residual read. The four controllers' weights are stacked, so their projections run as batched GEMMs. The merge (`ops/loop.py`) runs in FP32 without FMA contraction, as the reference, fused with the sublayer's RMSNorm.
- **Fused kernels** (`csrc/inkling2/`): `conv_mix`, `allreduce_conv_mix` and `seq_parallel` now support hidden size 2,304 as well as 4,608, and return the FP32 mix before the RMSNorm for message blends. The loop model uses them at every TP size; it does not use sequence parallelism.
- **Prefill:** from 2,048 tokens, the attention prologue's q/r work runs in its own launch beside the K/V convolutions (an 8K prefill at 51K context: 120.5 → 116.1 ms on GB200).
- **Expert GEMM operand sizing** (`ops/trtllm_bmm.py`, `ops/moe.py`, `ops/activation.py`): Inkling 2 calls the TRT-LLM-gen batched GEMMs directly (its activation, routing-weight placement and per-row activation scales do not fit FlashInfer's fused MoE). Every activation, block-scale, row-scale and output buffer of those GEMMs is now allocated with at least 128 KiB behind its base, the rule FlashInfer's MoE launchers apply to the same kernels (`maybeGetMinTokenCount`; see flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4319), since the kernels' TMA accesses can reach that far however few rows are used. Previously, small batches allocated exactly the planned rows, under 128 KiB. This also applies to Inkling 2 Small.
  - Motivation: the B200 CI job faulted (`CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT`) in the expert GEMM's TMA load during warmup of the DSpark cases of `test_tiny_model_generates`, which of the looped and non-looped models faulted depending on the batch budget. It does not reproduce on GB200, including with each GEMM operand placed flush against unmapped memory, so this change follows the kernels' documented contract and is confirmed only once the B200 job passes.
  - `test_moe.py::test_gemm_operands_span_128kib` checks the allocation rule; `test_tiny_model_generates` keeps the 256-token batch budget on all platforms; `test_tiny_model_routed_experts` allows its reference hook's host copy under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.
  - Performance: unchanged (see Validation).
- **Other changes:** SM120/SM121 kernels for DGX Spark, and routed-expert capture with one row per layer visit.
- **Config:** looped checkpoints must declare `model_type: inkling2_loop` and `architectures: [Inkling2LoopForConditionalGeneration]`, as the reference requires.
- **Docs:** Inkling 2 Mini is added to the supported models.
